historical_claims.anchor: The method of bounded differences turns such stability into a concentration inequality.
The Azuma–Hoeffding inequality applies to martingales with almost-surely bounded increments.
Variance-aware martingale inequalities, including Freedman's inequality, incorporate the sum of conditional variances along with a bound on positive increments.
A mixing condition can control those covariance terms or support a concentration inequality, often with constants depending on a mixing time or spectral gap.

description: Introduces concentration inequalities for dependent variables through bounded differences and martingale techniques, showing how structural controls can replace full independence.
